title: Runtime LTS drift detector + staging smoke/perf bench
creator: Maya Chen
description: Implement a lightweight LTS drift detector plus a staging bench that exercises smoke tests and targeted perf probes. The detector compares a candidate build against the pinned LTS baseline across: latency (P50/P95), throughput, token-level fidelity (token-diff), and a small semantic eval over golden prompts. The staging bench simulates KV-cache warmup, short/long sequence mixes, and quantization probe vectors to reveal regressions that only show under typical traffic shapes.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Preflight job runs in staging and produces a machine-readable report containing P50/P95 latency, throughput, token-diff rate, semantic-eval delta versus LTS baseline. 2) Gate config supports rules: latency_p95 <= baseline * 1.10 -> fail, throughput >= baseline * 0.95 -> warn, token_diff <= 0.2% -> fail, eval_drop <= 0.5 -> warn. 3) Bench completes in <= 6 minutes for quick preflight; longer nightly sweep left to regression pipeline. 4) Reporter artifacts uploaded to S3 and linked to rollout UI; hard gate failures automatically flag the release. 5) Runbook and playbook for on-call triage and manual rollback included.
notes: 2026-02-26: Spike showed KV warmup transitions can induce 6-10% latency variance on quantized paths for short sequences.
2026-03-02: Chose hybrid fidelity metric (token-diff + semantic eval) instead of raw n-gram scores to account for open model variance.
Bench design trade-off: sample golden prompts and truncate sequences to keep run time short; delegate exhaustive permutations to nightly regression runs.
Integration plan: report verdicts to rollout UI via annotation API and write gate outcomes to metadata store for automated rollouts.
Security note: staging job will use ephemeral credentials and LTS fixtures to avoid exposing customer data.
Operational constraint: job must include circuit-breaker to abort if GPU/CPU steal > 25% to avoid impacting shared staging tenants.
